steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This is the breeze from Old Siesta...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This is where the sea fowlbeasts come to make their home, isn't it?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Grandpa... I found it... after all this time, I've finally...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Siesta—I'm back—!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Let's leave all the bad in the past! No more troubles!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: It's all good days ahead from here on!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Wh-What?!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: That's my resume! Why is it in the trash?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Didn't you say you tried everything, but there just wasn't a suitable opportunity for me?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But nobody even opened my portfolio before it went into the trash with my resume!

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Please, calm down, Ann-Maier.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: I said I would try, as the Siesta HR Office does for every job applicant.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: But I can't help it that no one is interested in working with you.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Why doesn't anyone want to hire me?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: You can say it straight. No need to worry about my feelings. It's the only way I'll improve.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Just tell me what I need to work on. I won't disappoint you!

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Alright... I'll tell you, but it's not an easy thing to change.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: The issue is—

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: You're too unlucky.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: You see this mountain of documents? That's the resumes I received today, alone! How am I supposed to read through all that?

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: And so, what I do is—
The clerk takes a stack out of the pile and throws them into the trash. The pile of papers gets a little thinner.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Y-You didn't even glance them!

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: I only have so much energy.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But reading resumes is your job!

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: No, my job is to pick the right talents for prospective employers.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: And our most important standard, right now, is whether the applicant can bring good luck to those employers.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Siesta has had enough misfortune these past few years. The last thing that employers want is another accident.

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: And you just had the bad luck of having your resume thrown in the trash... why would an employer want to hire someone as jinxed as you?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: J-Jinxed? This is ridiculous...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I came here full of hope and expectation...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I would have been happy to end up on a tiny engineering team, even an assistant post on an intern's wages.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But you're saying no one wants to hire me because I'm too unlucky?!

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Hey, what are you doing? Calm down—

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Just you wait! I'll find my own way! I'll show you... I'll find my own projects, form my own team!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Who needs your... your...

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Hey! Wait...

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: Ann-Maier, calm down, don't—

steps.name: Office Clerk
steps.text: My trash can! You need to pay for that!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I'm not paying for one stinking fowlbeast egg!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Deep breaths... deep breaths...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Just a lazy city hall clerk. That doesn't prove anything.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: If Siesta's official channels won't work, I can look for private construction firms.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: And if that doesn't work either, I can go knock on some doors up and down the streets.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: There are construction projects everywhere in Siesta. There's got to be a place that'll take me... right?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Is Siesta really like grandpa said?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Try some local Siestan snacks and turn that frown upside-down!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: My pies are a regular on 'Siesta's Best Eats'!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Best Eats?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Here! First-time customers get one free!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Oh, thanks!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: (Bites)

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Er...
Her brow furrows slightly.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Wh-What is it? Is it not to your taste?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Oh, no, it's great.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I just didn't expect it to be so... sweet.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I've never had sour orange pies this sweet.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: This isn't a sour orange pie. It's a sweet orange pie.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Sweet orange pie?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Just a sour orange pie with more sweet fillings, really.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But it's the sour kind that's Siesta's specialty, isn't it? That's what grandpa always used to make.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: He only used oranges that were completely green, without a single hint of yellow.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: And certainly no sweet fillings either...

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Ooh, now that's the classic, old-timey recipe for the real die-hards.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Was your grandpa Siestan?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I'm Siestan too.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: I guess you haven't been back in a while.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: My family moved to Columbia when I was little.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: No wonder why you sound so Columbian.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Hank! One sweet orange pie, please!

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Back again, Lut?

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Shh, don't tell Harley!

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: (Whisper) The sweetest kind, please!

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Alright, here you go.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Thanks, Hank!
The boy grabs the bag and runs away.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: So much honey...

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Not just that. That one had a triple serving of condensed milk, and caramel on the bottom.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: No wonder it's so sweet. That's not a sour orange pie anymore, is it?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: What am I supposed to do about it?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: The kids like it sweet, and so do the tourists. Sour orange pies have to change too, if I want to sell them.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: It's not your granddaddy's Siesta anymore...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I guess you're right.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This place is very different from the Siesta that Grandpa used to talk about.
Some things stay the same.
Siestans have accepted new tastes, but sometimes we long for the tastes of the past too.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Hey, if it isn't the up-and-coming star of city hall.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Didn't think you'd have time for my humble little stall.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Just passing by... I'll have one sour orange pie, please, Hank.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Spare me the formalities. It didn't use to be a thing back in our Old Siesta days.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: (This man is from city hall too...)

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm glad we can still get along like the old days, now that all the old shops on Fashion Street are completely unrecognizable.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Well, the rebuilding has gone alright.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: We got compensated for business interruption, and we've heard about the coming subsidies. We're not complaining.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: People with too much time on their hands, like me, can set up a stall to have something to do.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Here, your sour orange pie, sour enough to make your teeth fall off. I know the tastes of Fashion Street.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: ...I appreciate everyone's cooperation.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Thanks, Hank.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Excuse me.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Oh? You're still here?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Is construction still going on at the Fashion Street that you were talking about?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Around the clock.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Word on the street is that a couple of foreign moguls are waiting for construction to finish before building Terra's biggest water park in the area.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You're exaggerating, Hank...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: It's just to help the people of the old district get used to life on the nomadic city.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Siesta can't wallow in the memories of old forever, after all.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: (Siesta's past can still be seen in that Fashion Street.)

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: (But even this little fragment of memory will...)

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Is Fashion Street still hiring workers?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Easy, easy... careful, kids, this stuff is precious!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I told you we can't send all of this to that new warehouse... they're not... I'm not ready.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: They shouldn't be hidden away like this. Don't you agree, my love?

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: It's all good, honey.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: They won't be useful until our 'Lava Fissure' musical BBQ is open for business, will they?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: These were passed down to me from my mother, who inherited it from her own mother.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I polish them regularly. You can hear them ring when you knock on them!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I just can't...

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Don't worry! We've got all your guitars, drums, and those... are they xylophones or harps? Anyway, we've got them all wrapped up.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Shock-absorbing pads all around, and watertight wrappings that won't let the slightest bit of moisture in.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: They'll be perfectly in tune when your, er, musical BBQ opens. You can count on us!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I'm not talking about the instruments!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I'm talking about the barbecue racks! Did you wrap them up properly too?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Huh...? Those weren't for scrap?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Wh-What did you just say?!

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: So this is Fashion Street...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Looks like there was a bit of misunderstanding with that shop?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: The argument seems to be getting heated. Should we intervene?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Don't worry, it's not an argument. The residents just need time to say goodbye to the 'good ol' days'.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: After all, most shops on this street are older than you and me put together.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I've heard stories about that street, on the shores of Siesta.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Barbecue racks on the beach underneath colorful beach umbrellas, music loud enough to drown out the waves, all the residents gathered for the party.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Grandpa said Siesta wasn't so built-up back then. There were few beautiful high-risers, and equally few tourists...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But the people were no less happy back then.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Your grandfather and mine would have a lot to talk about, if they ever met.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Your grandfather?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: He was an eccentric optimist.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Most old people are. A little weird, but always optimistic... even though they had their share of problems to deal with when they were young.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Compared to that, I'm...
She gazes at the center of the city—
Beautiful high-risers line the skyline in the distance, while cars drive through clean and broad streets.
Many tourists come and go, a few trendily-dressed figures taking pictures of volcano graffiti at a corner.
It is the Siesta that her grandfather had dreamt about.
But to her, everything seems so distant, as though she was only halfway here.
For a moment, she felt like there was a whole sour orange stuck in her throat.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Speaking of which—

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: My colleagues were talking about a 'the trash can crusher' in the city hall group chat.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I heard about the young girl's windy path to Siesta.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: She must be quite the optimist, to keep going despite all the trials and tribulations. Admirable.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Now that I think about it, her name was also Ann-Maier. What a coincidence, huh?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I got carried away... I'm planning to apologize to that clerk later.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I'm sorry! I'll pay for whatever damage I caused.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm not here to collect damages.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I just happened to pass by the sour orange pie stall, and I just happened to be in a position to pick up a mess left by an irresponsible coworker—

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Helping a young woman who came to Siesta looking for a job.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: After all, I know how it feels to have plenty of talent, but no place to use it.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Thank you, Mr. Costa...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But what do I do?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: What do you want to do?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: What... do I want to do?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I wanted to ask if there were any shops on Fashion Street that needed a hand in their rebuilding...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But what happened at the instrument shop as I passed by made me worry whether I could do a good job.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Because I know nothing about New Siesta, and what I know about Old Siesta is limited to the stories my grandpa told me.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: From the Obsidian Festival, to the advent of the nomadic city, to the farewell party for Mount Siesta that I've heard so many people talk about in my time here...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I missed so much... I don't know what Siesta needs today.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You don't.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: So what?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I doubt your grandfather knew much about the tiny coastal town when he visited for the first time.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Are you not in the same boat as he was?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You have plenty of time to learn more about this city.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I'm not sure I can... I've wasted so much time.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Stop thinking. Let's go.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: To do what you came to do in the first place.
The sound of construction on Fashion Street begins to fade as night falls, replaced by the excited atmosphere of the inhabitants gathering and enjoying themselves.
Except—

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This is...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Even the sign outside is gone from this shop. This scent...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Coffee?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Yes, this used to be a cafe.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: This will be your workplace for a while.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Work here? Am I supposed to rebuild the shop?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But where's the owner? Does he have a plan for rebuilding?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Will this place still be a cafe when it's rebuilt?
After a brief silence, the city hall official gives his answer.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: The owner is gone. There's no one to inherit this shop. Your job is not to rebuild it.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Not rebuild? Then...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You must tear it down.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Tear it down?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: All of it? The entire shop?
The official nods.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I... I can't do that...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: There will be other workers. Plenty of manpower.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Your wages will be paid out of the city hall's Fashion Street rebuilding project.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: If you accept this job, I will draft an employment contract for you on behalf of city hall that will protect the rights that you are entitled to.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: No, that's not what I mean... I mean this shop.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: The furniture, the shelves... the previous owner really took care of them.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: It would be such a shame to tear it all down... all the sweet memories of Old Siesta.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Have you ever heard about the story of the wayfowl and homefowl?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Wayfowl... homefowl?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: The words sound familiar... what do they mean?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: When I was little, my grandfather told me stories of a kind of fowlbeast.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Legends say that an ancient kind of fowlbeast used to live on that beach.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Beach... you mean Old Siesta?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: But Old Siesta didn't exist when those fowlbeasts filled the skies and forests.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Perhaps not even Mount Siesta did.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: It was that long ago? Even the volcano didn't exist yet?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: What's the story with those fowlbeasts?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Once upon a time, they were not a single kind of fowlbeast.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: They were a complex community, comprising many different species of migratory fowlbeasts, 'wayfowls' that came from all over the land, and its members took many different forms and habits.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: At first, they gathered in the woods by the beach.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Sometimes they fought one another. Some left, while others stayed, building their nests and nursing the next generation together.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Eventually, they became one species that ate the same fruits and sang the same songs. They made their home here, and become 'homefowls'.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: My grandfather loved the story. He believed that these ancient fowlbeasts were like Siesta.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Can we still see these fowlbeasts today?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm afraid not... at the end of the story, a heavy rain that lasted many years caused the sea to rise and flood the woods where they made their home.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: That was the last that anyone knew of those fowlbeasts.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Ann-Maier?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I... I'm fine.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: It's just a legend.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: In reality, Siesta has been much more fortunate than those fowlbeasts.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I know...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I just remembered where I heard the words 'wayfowl' and 'homefowl'.

steps.name: Young Girl
steps.text: Grandpa, what's that word on this can of sour orange sauce?

steps.name: Kindly Old Man
steps.text: It says 'Siesta'.

steps.name: Young Girl
steps.text: Siesta? What's Siesta?

steps.name: Kindly Old Man
steps.text: Oh my, have you forgotten already, Ann-Maier?

steps.name: Kindly Old Man
steps.text: Siesta is an orange that's not yet ripe.

steps.name: Kindly Old Man
steps.text: Siesta made wayfowls settle down and become homefowls. Siesta is the home that we built.

steps.name: Young Girl
steps.text: Wayfowl... homefowl? I don't understand.

steps.name: Kindly Old Man
steps.text: Someday you will, little one. Someday.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: So your grandfather once told a similar story...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Sorry, Mr. Costa... I keep thinking back to the past.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I know the feeling.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I often think back to the times that I spent with my grandfather.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: But the memories that don't fade also don't impede my ability to look forward.
She hears the sound of music and casts her gaze in the direction of the sound.
The scarlet door of the instrument shop is wide open, and dim lights fall upon packaging boxes big and small.
The owners sit with the workers on the ground, holding various instruments in their hands from guitars to tambourines to maracas, to folk instruments the names of which she does not know.
A dissonant note causes everyone to stop.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey, who played it wrong this time?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Oh, maybe it was me...

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: But this is how it goes back at my hometown...

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Let's all adjust, then.
Some changed the chord, some slowed down the rhythm. The worker does not change his notes, but the phrase is once again in harmony.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: One more time. Three, two, one—

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: It's the calluses on our hands, the brick dust on our shoulders♪

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: The wine of our meeting, the song of our parting♪

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: This is Siesta, this is home♪

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This is Siesta...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Yes, this is Siesta.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Hello?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Yes, this is Ann-Maier...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: You say you got me an interview with a construction company by way of apology?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Oh, I'm afraid I'll have to decline.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: No, I was at fault for what happened today, too. Thank you very much. Hope to talk to you again.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: From city hall?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Why did you turn it down?

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: Maybe because I understand what wayfowl and homefowl mean now... well, maybe not all of it...

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: But like you said, I have time to learn about the city... I should slow down and take it all in.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: That's why I'll take this job.
She looks at the dusty shop.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: I'll clear out the old furniture and repaint the walls within the apportioned time, restoring this house to its former glory.

steps.name: Ann-Maier
steps.text: This is my first job in Siesta.
